fixtures.basis: Not determined. Atlanta's amendments to the state plumbing and building codes sit in appendices of its Code of Ordinances on Municode, which could not be opened, and no readable copy was found. Nothing found in search results points to an Atlanta change to the toilet-count table: the City's codes page (search result only) lists the 2024 International Plumbing Code 'with Georgia Amendments' and no city amendment. restrooms_city.note: No Atlanta ordinance or code amendment on single-user restroom signs or shared all-gender rooms in private buildings was found (one web search; the Code of Ordinances could not be opened). Search results show a 2021 City Council paper and a mayoral administrative order designating single-occupancy restrooms in City-owned facilities as 'All Gender' (https://citycouncil.atlantaga.gov/home/showpublisheddocument/6949/637598679852100000, not opened, 403). That concerns the City's own buildings and adds nothing for other owners; the state rule already requires a one-person room to be open to everyone.

page.meta: Commercial bathroom partitions delivered to Atlanta job sites. Price your restroom, pick the right material and see the Atlanta and Georgia rules.
page.lead: Commercial bathroom partitions for Atlanta offices, schools, hotels and distribution centers, shipped by freight to your job site.
page.stall_bullet: - **How many stalls:** Georgia's plumbing rules set the number of toilets by how many people use the building, and Atlanta enforces them. The table below shows what that means.
page.permit_bullet: - **Permits:** Atlanta requires a permit for new construction and for specific alterations to existing buildings, including structural, plumbing, mechanical and electrical changes. The city's permit guidance doesn't name toilet partitions, so ask the Atlanta Office of Buildings whether your replacement needs one. Work at the airport needs the Department of Aviation's approval before plans go to the Office of Buildings. You don't need a permit to buy partitions.
page.stalls_after: These are state minimums for the whole building. A city may set stricter ones, so confirm the count with the Atlanta Office of Buildings. An office that holds 25 people or fewer, or any space that holds 15 or fewer, may use one restroom for everyone.
page.capacity: To find your building's capacity, the building rules count an office at one person per 150 square feet of floor, a restaurant dining room at one per 15 square feet and a classroom at one per 20. Your architect or the Atlanta Office of Buildings sets the final number.
page.install_rule: Work done under an Atlanta permit must be done by a holder of a valid City of Atlanta business license. Georgia licenses general contractors, and limited specialty trade work may be exempt, so confirm with the Georgia State Licensing Board for Residential and General Contractors whether your installer needs a state license. You don't need a permit to buy partitions.
page.faq_install_extra: A contractor who works under an Atlanta permit needs a City of Atlanta business license.
page.public_jobs_bullet: - **Public jobs:** Georgia has no state wage law for public construction, so a set wage applies only on federally funded projects, under federal law. For a carpenter on building work in Fulton County that rate is $17.48 an hour, with no benefits amount listed.
page.sales_tax_bullet: - **Sales tax:** 8.9% in Atlanta: 4% state, 1% local option, 1% schools, 1.5% MARTA, 1% city and 0.4% city transportation tax.
page.buyers_extra: - **Hotels, stadiums and convention venues:** finishes that match the property in guest-facing restrooms, HDPE or phenolic where crowds and frequent washdown are hard on stalls.

page.official_names: - The rules by their official names: 2010 ADA Standards for Accessible Design; Georgia Accessibility Code (Rules of the Safety Fire Commissioner, Chapter 120-3-20, effective January 1, 2015); Georgia State Minimum Standard Building Code (2024 International Building Code with Georgia Amendments, effective January 1, 2026) and Georgia State Minimum Standard Plumbing Code (2024 International Plumbing Code with Georgia Amendments, effective January 1, 2026), enforced in Atlanta by the Office of Buildings; Atlanta Code of Ordinances, Part III, Appendix A (Building Code Amendments), Chapter I, for permits; NFPA 286 for HDPE.
